recommendation: Keep this audit commit as-is. Do not re-add valueset-special-status or duplicate the warning on every fhir-types value set unless FHIR-I or Vocabulary makes a new decision; the current source conveys the version-specific terminology behavior without depending on the deprecated extension.
issue_request: FHIR-14864 was a Published/Not Persuasive with Modification FHIR-I change request arguing that the normative all-types value set could not safely remain normative because future FHIR versions might rename immature resources such as BodySite to BodyStructure. The approved resolution kept the terminology normative but required explanatory text about versioned code system contents and forwards/backwards compatibility.
initial_application: The issue was applied in SVN revision 13090, represented in Git as 3e15b565783d5d32d9943f5be5b52d8bfb1af308. That commit added the res-status-special placeholder to code system and value set templates and changed the all-types/data-types/resource-types binding descriptions to say they are lists defined by this version of FHIR.
additional_context: The old all-types family has since been refactored into fhir-types and related version-specific/version-independent type value sets. OperationDefinition.parameter.type and OperationDefinition.parameter.allowedType now bind to ValueSet/fhir-types with this-version wording. FHIR-40706 later deprecated valueset-special-status; an existing combined-branch reconciliation removed that deprecated extension use from fhir-types while preserving the FHIR-14864 warning in CodeSystem.description.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. The current fhir-types CodeSystem says it is normative, generated from the specification, has a fixed definition, and has contents that change from version to version. OperationDefinition still describes fhir-types as the types defined in this version of FHIR, and current old/version-independent type terminology covers renamed/deleted resource names.

related_jiras.note: Deprecated valueset-special-status, the historical carrier for part of the FHIR-14864 warning; an existing reconciliation preserved that warning in CodeSystem.description instead.
Refactored the type terminology family around fhir-types/resource-types, affecting how the original all-types terminology appears in current source.

evidence_items.summary: Published/Not Persuasive with Modification issue objected to normative all-types because resource names can change, but resolved to keep it normative and add explanatory versioning/compatibility text.
evidence_items.learned: The final decision requires preserving implementer guidance about versioned terminology contents, not removing normative status.
